Seminar Title:

Numerical Investigation of Heat Transfer Enhancement and Thermal Safety in Lithium-ion Battery Systems

Seminar Type:

Manoj Kumar Moharana

Abstract:

Thermal management is essential for maintaining the performance, durability and safety of lithium-ion batteries, particularly under high-rate operation and abusive conditions. This thesis develops and evaluates a sequence of computational battery thermal management strategies, progressing from thermo-hydrodynamic optimisation of minichannel cold plates to battery integrated liquid cooling, thermal-runaway mitigation and, finally, a lightweight hybrid phase change material (PCM)&ndashair cooling system. Initially, a conventional circuitous minichannel cold plate is modified by incorporating flow fragmentation, multiple inlets and outlets, and various branching arrangements. Three-dimensional conjugate heat-transfer simulations show that the fragmented designs shorten the coolant flow path, reduce hydraulic losses and improve temperature uniformity. The study further demonstrates that cold-plate optimisation must simultaneously consider heat transfer, temperature uniformity, pressure drop and pumping requirement rather than relying on a single thermal metric. The improved concept is subsequently coupled with a transient MSMD&ndashNTGK lithium-ion battery model. Among the investigated flow configurations, the D3FF fragmented design provides the best overall thermal response, reducing the pressure drop by 68.14%, the maximum temperature rise by approximately 37.5%, and the battery temperature difference to 1.545 K, which is 24.45% lower than the corresponding conventional configuration. The developed cooling strategy is further examined under nail-penetration-induced thermal runaway in a 1P14S battery module. The results show that middle-edge penetrations are more severe than corner-edge cases, while penetration depth has a stronger influence on thermal runaway severity than penetration area. Increasing the triggering temperature from 330 to 530 K delays module-level propagation by approximately 40%. A combined mitigation strategy using a low-thermal-conductivity interface and fragmented minichannel cooling completely suppresses propagation to the neighbouring cell at Re = 400. To reduce the dependence on liquid-cooling hardware, a novel PCM&ndashaerofoil-fin-assisted forced air BTMS is finally proposed. The system integrates latent-heat storage, fin-assisted conduction and forced convection. Under 3C discharge, 298 K ambient temperature and (Re=100), the proposed configuration maintains the average battery temperature near 305 K with a PCM utilisation of approximately 0.83. Energy analysis shows that only 8.13% of the generated energy remains as battery sensible heat, while 29.91% is stored as PCM latent heat. Post-discharge PCM utilisation decreases from about 0.80 to 0.20 by 5000 s, indicating effective thermal regeneration. With a cooling-system mass of approximately 0.35 kg, a lower material cost than the PCM-only system, and the highest performance index of about 1.064, the proposed hybrid architecture offers a favourable balance among thermal performance, safety, regeneration capability, mass, and cost.
